summary: Prednicarbate is a non-halogenated medium-potency topical corticosteroid used to treat inflammatory and pruritic dermatoses such as atopic and contact dermatitis. Its diester structure is metabolized in the skin, giving good anti-inflammatory activity with a relatively favorable atrophy profile. It should be used in the smallest effective amount for the shortest time to limit local and systemic steroid effects.
indications: Relief of the inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses (e.g., atopic dermatitis, contact dermatitis)

moa: Prednicarbate is a corticosteroid diester that, after penetrating the skin, exerts anti-inflammatory, antipruritic and vasoconstrictive actions. Corticosteroids induce phospholipase-A2-inhibitory proteins (lipocortins), reducing release of arachidonic acid and downstream prostaglandins and leukotrienes, thereby suppressing the inflammatory response.

missed: If a regular application is missed, apply it when remembered; if it is nearly time for the next application, skip the missed one. Do not apply extra to make up.
overdose: Topical overuse can be absorbed systemically and produce reversible HPA-axis suppression or, rarely, features of hypercortisolism. Discontinue gradually if suppression is suspected and treat symptomatically.
